canonical_name: MiniSat 1.14 (2006) -- the small CDCL solver in its pre-2.0 form (Een & Sorensson)
lineage: SAT lineage, the PREDECESSOR of the vault's minisat-2.2.0: 1.14 is the version described in 'An Extensible SAT-solver' (SAT 2003) as it stood in 2006 -- ~600 lines of core, before 2.0's rewrite (SimpSolver, new restart/reduce policies). Beside zchaff-2007 (the rival it displaced) and 2.2.0 (its successor) the vault holds the transition.
compiler_or_interpreter: g++ 4.9 (docker gcc:4.9 -- the preserved historical toolchain used for 2.2.0) or g++ 12 (recorded)

example.output: SATISFIABLE / UNSATISFIABLE (ORACLE: agreement with 2.2.0, picosat, zchaff)

upstream_docs: Een & Sorensson, An Extensible SAT-solver, SAT 2003

human_capability_summary.built_to: be the smallest complete CDCL solver competitive with the large ones, so others could extend it
human_capability_summary.pressure: the SAT competitions; the size and opacity of Chaff-era solvers
human_capability_summary.success_means: correct SAT/UNSAT; extensibility that made it the base of a generation of solvers

human_failure_condition: a wrong answer; a heuristic regression versus rivals
behavioral_entry_point: compare decisions/conflicts on one CNF across minisat 1.14, 2.2.0 and zchaff

lineage_relations.note: direction: MiniSat superseded zChaff (recorded on both records)

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run minisat-1.14-2006
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: be the smallest complete CDCL solver competitive with the large ones, so others could extend it
